builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Sustainable Processing-in-DRAM Integration and Replacement for Transformer Inference Servers
summary: The paper evaluates replacing or augmenting GPU inference servers with Processing-in-DRAM (PID) accelerators, providing a carbon modeling framework covering embodied, idle, and active carbon plus an aging-aware replacement schedule over 10 years. Adoption costs are substantial: PID hardware is not commercially procurable for a small team, requires server-level integration paired with specific GPUs, and results depend strongly on GPU pairing, with HGX-H100 servers showing 5.4-5.9x higher total carbon than A100/H100 configurations. The findings can fail in practice because they are model-based projections rather than measurements from deployed PID systems, and the optimal replacement period depends on carbon-intensity assumptions and workload mix.
rationale: PID accelerators are unavailable to a reader with one 24 GB GPU or API-based inference, and the paper is a carbon modeling study rather than an actionable technique, so it is only worth monitoring as procurement-relevant research.
technique: Processing-in-DRAM carbon modeling for inference servers

Adoption costs are substantial: PID hardware is not commercially procurable for a small team, requires server-level integration paired with specific GPUs, and results depend strongly on GPU pairing, with HGX-H100 servers showing 5.4-5.9x higher total carbon than A100/H100 configurations. The findings can fail in practice because they are model-based projections rather than measurements from deployed PID systems, and the optimal replacement period depends on carbon-intensity assumptions and workload mix.
Total carbon reduced by up to 1.14x for encoder and 1.04x for decoder workloads versus GPU-only servers, with embodied carbon increasing by at most 2.5%
